meta.scope: app/ and tests/; core flows: checkout, invoicing, subscription renewal

conventions.idiom: Amounts are stored and passed between modules as integer yen
Report queries count distinct order ids, never payment rows

findings.title: The invoice rounds tax per line while the charge rounds it once, so the card is charged a different amount
findings.hazard: The amount charged to the card differs from the invoice total by up to one yen per line
findings.scenario: Any order with several lines whose tax has a fraction: three lines of 333 yen at 10%
findings.blast_radius: Checkout and subscription renewal both charge through charge.py; invoices and the accounting export read invoice.py
findings.trace: 1. app/billing/invoice.py:42 rounds each line's tax down and sums the lines. 2. app/payments/charge.py:88 sums the net lines, applies the rate once and rounds with Python's round() (half to even). 3. Both feed the customer: the invoice PDF and the card statement. 4. Fixes 9c1d2e4 and 5b7a0f3 refunded 1-yen differences by hand
findings.impact: Customers are charged one yen more than their invoice says; support refunds by hand and the accounting export disagrees with the payment provider
findings.exposure: Core flow checkout (money); 4 callers of charge.py; fixes 9c1d2e4 and 5b7a0f3 refunded mismatches in the window

counterexample.input: One order: three lines of 333 yen each, tax rate 10%
counterexample.expected: Invoice total and charged amount both 1,098 yen (tax 33 per line, rounded down)
counterexample.actual: Invoice total 1,098 yen; charged amount 1,099 yen (999 x 0.1 = 99.9, rounded to 100)
counterexample.oracle: docs/billing/tax.md:12 states tax is computed per line and rounded down

enforcement.gaps: The invoice test covers one-line orders only; nothing compares the charged amount with the invoice

findings.change_reason: charge.py:88 is shared by checkout and subscription renewal (4 callers); renewals will charge one yen less on some invoices, which finance must expect
invariants: For every order, the amount charged equals the invoice total
Tax is computed per line and rounded down, by one function every caller uses
steps: 1. Move per-line tax into billing.tax.line_tax, call it from invoice.py and charge.py, update the renewal tests that expected the old charge, and add a test: three lines of 333 yen at 10% give 1,098 yen on the invoice and in the charge (verify: the new test fails with the change reverted, at the charge assertion; the billing and renewal suites pass with it)
findings.fix: One rounding function, per line and down, used by both the invoice and the charge

validation.evidence: app/billing/invoice.py:42 floor per line; app/payments/charge.py:88 round(total * rate); git show 9c1d2e4 5b7a0f3 refund 1-yen differences

findings.title: Checkout preview hard-codes 10% tax while invoices use each shop's rate
findings.hazard: The tax rate is defined twice, and only the invoice follows the shop's rate
findings.scenario: A food shop on the 8% reduced rate: every customer of such a shop sees a preview total that differs from the invoice
findings.blast_radius: 1 module; the checkout preview every customer sees before paying
findings.trace: 1. app/checkout/preview.py:22 multiplies the total by the literal 1.1. 2. app/billing/invoice.py:18 reads shop.tax_rate. 3. Commit 2e4f6a1 (feat: per-shop tax rates, not a fix) moved the invoice to shop.tax_rate and left the preview alone. 4. db/seeds/shops.yml:12 and docs/billing/tax.md:5 show food shops at 8%
findings.impact: Customers of reduced-rate shops are shown a higher total before paying than they are invoiced
findings.exposure: Core flow checkout; food shops on 8% exist (db/seeds/shops.yml:12); 2 copies of the rate, one changed by 2e4f6a1; no support note or refund records the mismatch

counterexample.input: A shop with tax_rate 0.08, an order of 1,000 yen
counterexample.expected: Preview total 1,080 yen, as the invoice will show
counterexample.oracle: docs/billing/tax.md:5: each shop's rate applies to every price it shows or charges

enforcement.gaps: Every preview test uses a 10% shop, so the literal and the shop's rate always agree in the suite

invariants: Every price shown or charged uses the shop's tax_rate
For a shop at 8%, the preview of a 1,000 yen order is 1,080 yen
steps: 1. Replace the literal with shop.tax_rate through the billing tax module, with a preview test for an 8% shop (verify: the test gives 1,080 yen, and fails with the change reverted)
2. Search for other literal rates and route them the same way (verify: grep for 0.1 and 1.1 in app/ finds no tax use)
findings.fix: Read the rate from one place, the billing tax module

validation.evidence: app/checkout/preview.py:22 total * 1.1; app/billing/invoice.py:18 shop.tax_rate; git show 2e4f6a1 changes invoice.py only; db/seeds/shops.yml:12 tax_rate: 0.08

findings.title: Subscription renewal compares the server's UTC date with the customer's billing day
findings.hazard: On a JST billing day, renewal waits until 09:00 JST, when the server's UTC date catches up
findings.scenario: The renewal job runs hourly; on a customer's billing day it runs at 01:00 JST, when the server's date is still the day before
findings.blast_radius: 1 job; every subscription in a time zone ahead of UTC
findings.trace: 1. renew_subscriptions.py:12 takes date.today() on a server set to UTC (config/runtime.py:4). 2. :15 compares it with subscription.billing_day, stored as a JST calendar date. 3. Runs before 09:00 JST see yesterday's date
findings.impact: Renewals run up to nine hours late: customers keep access past the end of their period until 09:00 JST and are charged that much later; the hourly runs before 09:00 do nothing for them
findings.exposure: Core flow subscription renewal (money); every JST customer; no fix commit in the window

counterexample.input: billing_day 2026-11-01 (JST); the job runs at 2026-11-01 01:00 JST (2026-10-31 16:00 UTC)
counterexample.expected: The subscription renews on that run
counterexample.actual: date.today() is 2026-10-31, so it is skipped; it renews on the 09:00 JST run, when the UTC date becomes 2026-11-01
counterexample.oracle: docs/billing/subscriptions.md:9: renewal happens on the billing day in the customer's time zone

enforcement.gaps: The renewal test freezes time at 12:00 UTC, where UTC and JST agree on the date

invariants: A subscription renews on the first run on or after the start of its billing day in the customer's time zone
A run at 01:00 JST on the billing day renews it
steps: 1. Compute today in the customer's zone with zoneinfo and compare that with billing_day, with a test freezing time at 2026-10-31 16:00 UTC (verify: the test renews a 2026-11-01 JST subscription, and fails with the change reverted)
findings.fix: Compare billing_day with the date in the customer's time zone, not the server's

validation.evidence: app/jobs/renew_subscriptions.py:12 date.today(); config/runtime.py:4 TZ=UTC; tests/billing/test_renewal.py:14 freezes 12:00 UTC

findings.title: The monthly sales report counts an order once per payment, against the distinct-order rule
findings.hazard: Orders paid in two parts are counted twice
findings.scenario: Split payments, enabled in 2026-03, give an order two payment rows
findings.blast_radius: 1 internal report; finance reads it, nothing else consumes it
findings.trace: 1. queries.sql:12 joins orders to payments. 2. monthly_sales.py:27 counts the joined rows. 3. docs/adr/0007-reporting.md:7 requires counting distinct order ids
findings.impact: Order counts in the internal monthly report are overstated since 2026-03
findings.exposure: Non-core internal report; split payments are about 4% of orders (docs/ops/payments.md:20)

enforcement.gaps: The report has no test, and its fixture has no split payment

findings.change_reason: Reports for 2026-03 onwards were already sent to finance overstated; correcting them needs a re-run and a note to finance
steps: 1. Count distinct order ids, with a fixture order paid in two payments (verify: it counts once, and twice with the change reverted)

2. List the months since 2026-03 whose counts change, for the correction decision (verify: each listed month's difference equals its split-payment orders); re-sending them is finance's decision, not this step
findings.fix: Count distinct order ids, as ADR 0007 requires, and correct the reports already sent

validation.evidence: app/reports/monthly_sales.py:27 len(rows) over the join at app/reports/queries.sql:12; docs/adr/0007-reporting.md:7 requires COUNT(DISTINCT order_id)

findings.title: Legacy coupon code treats a zero discount as no discount given
findings.hazard: if discount: skips a recorded zero and falls back to the default
findings.trace: 1. coupons.py:31 tests the discount for truth. 2. No route, job or import reaches coupons.py
findings.impact: Code nothing calls cannot produce a wrong result
findings.fix: Hand to prune-scan as a removal candidate

validation.evidence: app/legacy/coupons.py:31 is reachable from nowhere; a search for coupons in app/ and tests/ returns only the file itself
